subject: B1 linear HDR output and shared sky lighting
interpretation: The baseline app was built from clean ce84658643077e2b7dbc27e15e6df37ef7d262b8 before production rendering edits. Its old runtimeDiffSha256 was taken at capture completion during source editing and is not a build identifier.
The final app includes the B1 changes in this evidence commit. after.servedScripts hashes identify the actual delivered JavaScript; its commit field identifies the pre-change HEAD only.

Bundled fixture hashes differ with their library dependency, while all checkpoint JSON bytes and camera/seed settings are identical. Paused material checkpoints are directly comparable; live movement/combat uses real timing and has different tick counts.
CPU samples time the main-thread HexMap frame. They do not include independent Worker CPU time or all React work. GPU queries cover projection, scene and final output and arrive asynchronously.

One short run per revision is evidence of cost and output on this machine, not a statistically established speedup or complete-game 60 FPS certification. Startup/loading spikes are outside the sampling windows.

Resource bytes are ledger estimates, not driver VRAM. Baseline ledger omitted the old default framebuffer and sky, while the new ledger includes HDR color/depth/MSAA and sky/PMREM; their difference is not a measured VRAM increase.
Input readings are repeated session diagnostic values rather than independently timestamped input events. Baseline input array was empty because the original sampler read the wrong snapshot field.
Final samples use a 512 MiB GPU ledger limit based on the observed approximately 390 MiB pinned working set; no sample exceeded that limit. The original limit was 256 MiB.
Compiler warnings are retained verbatim in the raw report; ANGLE reports an upstream PMREM loop precision warning. No page, console-error or GL_INVALID errors were observed.
No dynamic shadows, rebuilt shore materials, final character models or UI art are included. Those remain subsequent visual work.

artifacts.note: Local generated media are not committed; rerun the documented fixture against each build to reproduce them.

validation.rootUnit: 438 passed; the four affected rendering tests passed again after the final context-loss fix.
validation.appUnit: 543 passed; both browser-console tests passed after adding the precise constant-fold warning classification.
validation.rootBrowser: 27 passed in the full default-backend run; final D3D11 output, 500-replacement soak and ten-cycle context recovery all passed after the context-loss fix.
validation.appBrowser: Full D3D11 run: 44 passed, two failures. Invalid empty-affix inventory fixture corrected; old-context target deletion moved into the loss event. Both failed journeys then passed, covering all 46 cases.
failuresResolved: A single material registry restores lighting/fog hooks without retaining old wrappers.
Host targets are disposed while the context is lost; hardware restoration no longer deletes old framebuffer/renderbuffer handles.
validation.limitation: The default SwiftShader app run hit a 20-second travel-click timeout with approximately 2.3-second frames and was stopped. No software-rendering pass or compatibility claim is made.
